about.title: Women's health, without the rush
body: MotherCare was founded by Dr. Priya Nair after years of watching patients get 10-minute appointments for conversations that deserved much longer.
Every visit here — whether it's an annual exam, a pregnancy check-in, or a difficult fertility conversation — gets the time and care it actually needs.

faqs.question: Do you accept new obstetric patients?
faqs.answer: Yes, we welcome new prenatal patients — please book as early in pregnancy as possible.

faqs.question: Do you offer weekend appointments?

faqs.question: What insurance do you accept?

faqs.question: Can I bring a partner to appointments?
faqs.answer: Absolutely — partners and support people are always welcome at appointments.

blogPosts.title: What to Actually Expect at Your First Prenatal Visit
blogPosts.excerpt: A calm, honest walkthrough of what happens at your first appointment — and why it's longer than you might expect.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Hannah Oyelaran
content: Your first prenatal visit is typically longer than any other appointment in your pregnancy — usually 45 minutes to an hour — because there's a full history to cover.
Expect a detailed conversation about your health history, family history, and any medications, alongside initial bloodwork and, often, your first ultrasound.
This is also the visit to ask every question you've been holding onto — due date estimation, what to expect trimester by trimester, and anything you're anxious about.
There's no such thing as too small a question at this visit. If something feels worth asking, it's worth asking.
